data.traefik:
# Traefik reference config for tautulli, generated by the hub from its image.yml.
# Labels for the tautulli service in your compose file. Traefik's docker provider must reach the tautulli
# container on a shared network; the entrypoint websecure and the certificate resolver letsencrypt are
# examples from a typical Traefik setup. Replace example.com with your domain. Websockets need nothing extra.
services:
  tautulli:
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.services.tautulli.loadbalancer.server.port=8181
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli.rule=Host(`tautulli.example.com`)
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli.service=tautulli
      # Authentication: uncomment one; the middleware is defined in your Traefik config.
      # - traefik.http.routers.tautulli.middlewares=authelia@docker
      # - traefik.http.routers.tautulli.middlewares=authentik@docker
      # API paths stay open so client applications keep working.
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli-api.rule=Host(`tautulli.example.com`) && (PathPrefix(`/api`) || PathPrefix(`/newsletter`) || PathPrefix(`/image`))
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli-api.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli-api.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli-api.service=tautulli
      - traefik.http.routers.tautulli-api.priority=100
data.base_url_note: Settings → Web Interface → Show Advanced → HTTP Root, set to /tautulli
